title: NanoFlow: Towards Optimal Large Language Model Serving Throughput
technique: Intra-device parallelism: nano-batching and duplicated nano-operations overlapping compute, memory and network ops; MILP auto-search of pipeline; constant dense batch with chunked prefill

optimized_metrics.evidence: throughput has emerged as a key metric that determines serving systems' performance ... NanoFlow automatically identifies the number, size, ordering, and GPU resource allocation of nano-batches to minimize the execution time
NanoFlow, a serving framework that aims to maximize utilization of the workload's resource bottleneck, when considered as a whole.
We select the SLO for average normalized latency as 200ms following prior works [59], which is also the typical human reading speed
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: We select the SLO for average normalized latency as 200ms following prior works [59]

headline_claim.text: With practical workloads, NanoFlow provides 1.91× throughput boost compared to state-of-the-art serving systems, achieving between 50% to 72% of optimal throughput across popular models.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define throughput as the total throughput of serving, which is the number of tokens processed per second by both prefill and decode phases.
metric_definitions.notes: Counts input+output tokens; optimal measured per GPU (token/s/GPU); convertible to decode-only or req/s via p/(p+d) factors

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Optimal throughput (measured in token/s/GPU) is achieved when the most limited resource, i.e. compute, is fully utilized.
metric_definitions.notes: Analytical roofline-style upper bound (1857 tokens/s/GPU for LLaMA-2-70B on A100); results reported as fraction of optimal

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We then measure normalized latency by first calculating the end-to-end request latency divided by output length in tokens, then taking the average for all requests.
metric_definitions.notes: Mean of per-request E2E/output tokens; 200ms SLO on the mean (not a per-request or tail SLO)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: decoding throughput (decode output per second) is d/(p+d) × Throughput_total, and request per second is 1/(p+d) × Throughput_total.
to measure the total throughput defined as the total number of input and output tokens divided by the execution time

slo_spec: SLO on average normalized latency = 200 ms/token, following prior work [59] and typical human reading speed; maximum request rate sustained within it reported
load_regime: offline batch (throughput) plus Poisson (exponential interarrival) request-rate sweep on 5-min traces
tradeoff_acknowledged: At low request rates NanoFlow has comparable but slightly higher latency than baselines because it targets throughput and uses a large dense batch (2048); nano-batching duplicates ops and increases weight-load memory I/O.
extractor_notes: Design targets end-to-end serving throughput (and utilization as the mechanism), validated against an analytical optimum; not kernel speed per se, though the mechanism is kernel-level overlap (kernel interference modeled). Latency is only a constraint (mean normalized latency SLO). The P99 remark (1.07x of average) is an observation, not an optimized target. Throughput counts prefill+decode tokens.
